feature: Add Database Schema Documentation for Migrations
workflow_rationale: This is a documentation-only task that doesn't require multi-phase implementation or service coordination. The task involves creating comprehensive documentation for existing database migration files.

phases.name: Database Schema Documentation
phases.description: Create comprehensive DATABASE.md file documenting all migrations, schema design, and critical patterns

subtasks.description: Create DATABASE.md with overview and table of contents

verification.instructions: Verify DATABASE.md exists and has proper table of contents structure
Verify documentation includes organizations, organization_members, and categories tables with their columns, constraints, and relationships

subtasks.notes: Document: organizations table (id, name, slug, settings), organization_members table (user_id, organization_id, role), categories table structure

verification.instructions: Verify documentation explains: (1) Why UPDATE/DELETE are blocked, (2) INSERT-only pattern, (3) Turkish Trade Ministry compliance requirement, (4) How price history is preserved

subtasks.notes: Documented price_ledger immutability pattern in DATABASE.md. Included: (1) trigger code preventing UPDATE/DELETE, (2) INSERT-only pattern with examples, (3) Turkish Trade Ministry compliance requirements with specific regulations, (4) price history preservation queries, (5) RLS policies, (6) anti-patterns and best practices. Documentation follows the established pattern from section 001.

verification.instructions: Verify documentation explains: features table, plans table, subscriptions table, feature_overrides table, and their relationships

subtasks.notes: Documented package management system in DATABASE.md. Included comprehensive documentation for: (1) features table - platform features catalog with key, name, category, and metadata, (2) plans table - subscription plans (lite, professional, premium) with pricing and feature lists, (3) subscriptions table - organization subscriptions with status lifecycle (trial, active, expired, cancelled, suspended), (4) feature_overrides table - custom permissions for special cases with expiration and audit trail. Documentation includes table structures, important notes, example SQL queries, relationship diagrams, RLS policy strategy, common queries for feature access control, and anti-patterns. Follows the established pattern from sections 001 and 002.

verification.instructions: Verify documentation explains: tables table (for QR codes per table), service_requests table, and the waiter notification system

subtasks.notes: Successfully documented tables and service_requests tables in DATABASE.md. Included comprehensive documentation for QR code system, waiter notification system, request types, status workflow, Realtime integration, package limits, RLS policies, and anti-pattern warnings. Followed established documentation patterns from previous sections.

verification.instructions: Verify documentation explains: menu_snapshots table with SHA-256 hash, audit_logs table, and compliance purpose

subtasks.notes: Successfully documented audit and compliance system in DATABASE.md. Included comprehensive documentation for: (1) menu_snapshots table - captures menu state with SHA-256 hash for cryptographic verification, JSONB snapshot data structure, automatic trigger creation, hash verification queries, and compliance usage examples, (2) audit_logs table - immutable audit trail with INSERT-only pattern, standardized action types, automatic trigger-based logging, query examples for security analysis and compliance reporting. Documentation includes table structures, relationship diagrams, RLS policy strategy, anti-patterns, and important reminders. Follows the established pattern from sections 001-005.

verification.instructions: Verify documentation explains: current_prices view (how it gets latest price from ledger), and any other views with their purpose

subtasks.notes: Successfully documented database views in DATABASE.md. Included comprehensive documentation for: (1) current_prices VIEW - uses DISTINCT ON and ORDER BY to extract the latest price from immutable price_ledger for each product, (2) VIEW structure with all columns (product_id, price, effective_from, created_at, created_by, change_reason, previous_price), (3) SQL definition showing DISTINCT ON (product_id) and ORDER BY product_id, effective_from DESC pattern, (4) detailed explanation of how it works (4 steps), (5) reasons why this VIEW is needed (performance, simplicity, consistency, immutability preservation), (6) extensive usage examples (SQL and TypeScript/Supabase integration), (7) important notes about RLS, real-time updates, performance indexes, and historical price queries, (8) VIEW update instructions, (9) anti-patterns and correct patterns, (10) future views that could be added (active_subscriptions, organization_features, pending_service_requests, table_status_summary). Documentation follows the established pattern from sections 001-005.

verification.instructions: Verify documentation explains: RLS policy for each table, multi-tenant isolation strategy, how organization_members table is used in policies

subtasks.notes: Successfully documented RLS policies in DATABASE.md. Included comprehensive documentation for: (1) What RLS is and why it's critical for multi-tenant isolation - explaining how RLS works at database level to prevent cross-tenant data access, (2) Multi-tenant isolation strategy - explaining the 4-step flow from authentication to automatic filtering through organization_members table, (3) Two helper functions (auth.is_org_member and auth.user_org_ids) with SQL definitions, usage examples, and performance notes, (4) All 10 RLS policies documented individually with SQL code, explanations, TypeScript examples, and special notes (organizations, organization_members, categories, products, price_ledger, restaurant_tables, service_requests, menu_snapshots, audit_logs, subscriptions), (5) How organization_members table is used as the isolation boundary in all policies - explaining the role-based access control foundation, (6) Testing strategies with 3 concrete test scenarios (tenant isolation, authorization control, price_ledger immutability+RLS), (7) Anti-patterns section with 3 common mistakes and correct approaches (client-side filtering, service role misuse, helper function misuse), (8) Important reminders about RLS best practices, (9) Table summary showing RLS status and policy types for all tables, (10) External documentation links. Documentation includes 688 lines, follows established patterns from previous sections, uses Turkish language throughout, and covers all verification requirements.

verification.instructions: Verify documentation explains: trigger function, when it fires, what snapshot data includes, SHA-256 calculation

subtasks.notes: Successfully documented auto-snapshot trigger in DATABASE.md. Included comprehensive documentation for: (1) create_menu_snapshot() trigger function - full SQL definition with DECLARE variables (v_snapshot_data, v_snapshot_hash, v_organization_id), function parameters table (NEW record details), and function variables table, (2) auto_create_menu_snapshot trigger definition - AFTER INSERT on price_ledger, FOR EACH ROW execution, with detailed trigger properties table explaining timing, event, level, and function, (3) When the trigger fires - 3 scenarios with SQL examples (single product price change, bulk price updates, new product with initial price), plus list of when trigger does NOT fire, (4) Complete snapshot_data JSONB structure - full JSON example with categories array containing products with all fields (id, name, description, current_price, is_available, display_order, image_url), plus summary object with total counts and snapshot_version, detailed table explaining each field with type and examples, important details about current_price source, sorting, NULL values, and versioning, (5) SHA-256 hash calculation - 3-step process (JSONB→text, SHA-256 digest binary, hex encode), hash calculation formula, hash properties table (algorithm, output length, hex length, deterministic, collision resistant), hash verification SQL example with expected results, and hash usage areas (legal audit, data integrity, fraud detection, compliance audit), (6) Metadata structure - JSON example, field descriptions table, usage purposes, and example query to find which price change triggered a snapshot, (7) Performance considerations - cost table (menu data collection, JSONB aggregate, SHA-256, snapshot insert), bulk update warnings with solutions (disable trigger temporarily, use scheduled snapshots), and best practices list, (8) Trigger lifecycle and management - trigger status check query, disable/enable commands, drop/recreate trigger, and function update example, (9) Error handling and rollback - 3 scenarios with SQL examples (snapshot INSERT failure, organization_id not found, foreign key error), all showing automatic rollback behavior with transaction safety guarantees, (10) Anti-patterns and best practices - 4 examples showing wrong vs correct approaches (duplicate manual INSERT, bulk operations without disabling trigger, updating snapshot hash, manual hash changes), (11) Related tables and relationships - ASCII diagram showing flow from price_ledger INSERT through trigger to menu_snapshots, plus table showing all related tables with their roles, (12) Important reminders - 7 key points about trigger automation, transaction safety, performance, hash validation, compliance, monitoring, and version control. Documentation spans 670 lines, follows established patterns from previous sections (001-007), uses Turkish language throughout, and covers all 4 verification requirements: trigger function explanation, when it fires, snapshot data contents, and SHA-256 calculation details.
